query_text: A final-year student (last two semesters) has a GPA of 1.8 and is under academic probation. Can she register 21 credit hours under the final-year load exception, or does the probation cap apply?
A student's absence reaches 18% of course hours, but 5 percentage points of that absence are covered by a stamped medical excuse. Is the student forced to withdraw under the 15% rule?

A student wants to repeat a course he already passed to raise his GPA, but it has been 14 months (more than one academic year) since he passed it. He is currently on academic probation and his advisor supports the repeat. Is this allowed?
A student fails the final exam with only 25% of the exam mark, but her combined coursework score (30%+20%+10%) gives her an overall course percentage of 68%. Does she pass the course?

A student was given an Incomplete (I) grade after an accepted medical excuse, but records show she had only completed 55% of coursework marks (33/60) at the time, not the 60% required. Should the grade stand as (I) or convert to (F)?

A student who fails the exam-integrity offense of cheating (Article 24, offense #3) is also under academic probation with only 11 credit hours registered that semester. Does the probation's 12-hour cap protect any of his other courses from the two-adjacent-course 'W' penalty?
A student drops a course that has a co-registered prerequisite course in the same semester, intending to keep the prerequisite course. Is this permitted under the add/drop rules?

A student on the underachievement list (completed less than 50% of required hours) also has a GPA of 2.3, which is above the 2.0 probation threshold. Is she simultaneously subject to the academic probation load cap of 12 credit hours?

A graduating student who has not completed the prerequisite for one remaining required course wants to register for it in her final semester. Does the prerequisite rule in Article 8f block this, or does her final-year status create an exception?

A student who received a forced withdrawal (W) due to 16% unexcused absence wants to re-register for the same course next semester by only sitting the final exam, citing his strong grades in similar courses. Is this permitted?

A national swim-team athlete misses 22% of a course's sessions while representing her country at an international championship. Does the 20% mandatory-withdrawal rule in Article 17a force her withdrawal?

A College of Maritime Transport and Technology student misses 12% of her guided maritime training hours. Does the general course-attendance rule (mandatory withdrawal at 20%) or the training-specific rule (failure at 10%) govern her case?

A student wants her final exam paper remarked. She submits the appeal to her academic advisor 45 days after results were announced, rather than to the head of department within 30 days. Is the appeal valid under Article 18e?

A student achieves a final GPA of 3.35 with all passing grades except one course where she received an F in her second year, which she later repeated and passed. Does she qualify for an Honours degree under Article 19E?
A withdrawn course (grade W) and an audited course (grade Au) both appear on a student's transcript. Do either of these affect her cumulative GPA calculation under Article 19?

A student under academic probation argues that because he is a final-year student, the final-year exception in Article 8e should let him register 21 credit hours instead of the probation cap. His advisor disagrees. Whose position is correct?

A student claims that because his academic advisor personally recommended he take 15 credit hours this semester, the advisor's recommendation should override his 12-credit probation cap under Article 9. Is this claim valid?

A student argues that his final exam score of 28% should still count as passing because his overall course percentage of 71% clearly exceeds the department's typical passing bar. Does the overall high score override the final-exam floor in Article 18b?

A student who received two academic probation warnings argues that since he transferred to a new department after the second warning, the three-semester GPA recovery clock in Article 25a should restart entirely rather than apply to his standing at the new department. Is he correct?

A student argues her medical excuse should exempt her absences from counting toward the 20% mandatory-withdrawal ceiling entirely, since the excuse was approved and stamped by Academy Medical Services. Is this claim correct?

A student argues that because she is a graduating student, Article 8f's prerequisite exception should let her register for any remaining course without prior college review, since 'graduating students are an exception.' Is her reading correct?

A student who exceeded his allowed study period (double the original duration) argues that having a GPA of 2.4 should automatically grant him the one-final-chance extension under Article 16.2, since he clearly meets the GPA requirement. Is he correct?

A student argues that because the course-repeat cap under Article 12d allows repeating up to 5 passed courses for GPA improvement, and he has only repeated 3 so far, he should also be allowed to bypass the separate one-year time window in Article 12e for those repeats. Is this correct?

A student argues that submitting an appeal to the Academy President under Article 22 should let him retroactively change his officially recorded final grade average after graduation, since Article 22 allows appeals for 'special circumstances.' Is this valid?

A student argues that his strong extracurricular record and national sports representation (Article 17c) should exempt him from the disciplinary penalty for cheating (Article 24, offense #3) since both are forms of 'special status.' Is this reasoning valid?

A student claims that because Article 26 allows appealing disciplinary penalties, an appeal automatically suspends the penalty (e.g., the F grade from cheating) until the appeal is resolved. Is this correct?

A student on academic probation with advisor recommendation wants to both repeat a course beyond the 5-course cap (Article 12d) and beyond the one-year window (Article 12e) in the same semester, arguing the probation-plus-advisor exception in Article 12e should also waive the 5-course cap in Article 12d. Is this correct?

A student argues that because he plays for a national sports team (Article 17c), he should also be exempt from the mandatory final-exam 30% floor (Article 18b) during the championship period, since both rules involve 'exceptional circumstances.' Is this valid?

A student argues that his honours-track GPA of 3.4 should let him bypass the maximum academic load of 18 credit hours in Article 8a, since Article 8d already lets high-GPA students (3.00+) add one extra course. Is his reasoning correct?

A student argues that since Article 11.4 disallows optional withdrawal from physical/leadership training courses, this should also mean these courses are exempt from the general forced-withdrawal attendance rule in Article 17a, since 'withdrawal' is mentioned in both. Is this correct?

A student is on academic probation (GPA 1.9), is in her final year, and has one unmet prerequisite for a required graduating course. What is her maximum allowed course load this semester, and can she register for the course with the unmet prerequisite?

A student has been on the underachievement list for two consecutive semesters (having completed less than 50% of required hours) and is now transferring to a new department. If her GPA at the new department stays at 1.85 through her third semester there, what happens under the regulations?

A student receives a forced withdrawal (W) due to 17% unexcused absence in a core course she had already failed once before. When she re-registers next semester, what grade ceiling and attendance requirement apply if she passes this time?

A student exceeded the maximum study period (double her college's normal duration), has completed 82% of her required hours, holds a GPA of 2.1, and has a pending military-service deferral. Walk through what determines whether she is expelled or granted an extension.

A student under probation with a mandatory advisor-recommended 12-hour load wants to repeat two courses she already passed (to raise her GPA), where one course was passed 8 months ago and the other 16 months ago. Which repeats are permitted, and under what combined conditions?

A student commits the disciplinary offense of offending the invigilator (Article 24 offense #4) while simultaneously under academic probation with 3 courses registered at exactly her 12-hour cap. What is her academic status for this semester and next?

A College of Maritime Transport and Technology final-year student is under academic probation, has 11% absence in her guided maritime training, and wants to increase her academic load using the final-year allowance. Determine her load cap and training status.

A student fails a core course for the second time on a repeat attempt, is under academic probation, and this repeat course also has a co-registered prerequisite pairing with another course. If she wants to drop the repeat course now, what happens to her GPA, her load, and the paired course?

A student has a final GPA of 3.4 upon meeting all graduation requirements, but discovers she received an F in one course during her second year, which she repeated and passed with a B. She wants to know if she qualifies for Honours, and separately, whether she can still improve her GPA now that she has graduated.

A student's absence reaches 21% in a course, of which 6 percentage points are from a properly stamped medical excuse covering a final-exam period, and she also submitted her exam-remarking appeal on day 32 after results were announced. Resolve all applicable outcomes.

A student is on academic probation for a second time and has just transferred to a new department per her advisor's guidance after her first probation's three-semester limit expired. She now also fails to meet the transferred department's admission GPA requirement retroactively assessed at transfer. What is her status?

A graduating student has one unmet prerequisite, is simultaneously under academic probation, and wants to register for both the prerequisite-exempt course and an additional course using the GPA≥3.00 extra-course allowance despite having a GPA of 1.95. Evaluate each request.

A student in the College of Engineering and Technology receives a 72% overall course score. Using the Engineering-specific grading table, determine her letter grade and GPA value, and explain whether the same percentage would map to a different letter grade under the general (non-Engineering) table.

A student on probation registers 12 credit hours (her legal maximum), then wants to add a course after week 2 while dropping a different course whose prerequisite is bundled with a third registered course. Trace the load, bundling, and probation implications.

A student fails all courses in a semester due to a disciplinary offense (offending the invigilator, Article 24 #4), had also been on academic probation before the incident, and her case is now with the Student Affairs Committee. If the Committee allows her to continue, what governs her subsequent semester's load and status?
